name: retry-backoff
title: Cap retry backoff
description: Committed branch with an added, modified, deleted, and renamed file. Tours in diff mode.

repo.headMessage: Cap retry backoff and sleep between attempts

README.md: A tiny retry helper used by the kanko simulator.
Nothing in this file is part of the reviewed change.
docs/RETRY.md: Use `withRetry(fn, attempts)` to retry a flaky call.
Attempts run back to back with no delay.
Retry idempotent reads and writes that carry an idempotency key.
Never retry a request that failed validation; it will fail again.
See src/retry.js for the implementation and its tests.

Attempts back off exponentially, capped at `policy.maxMs`.

thesis: Retries now back off exponentially with a cap instead of hammering the dependency in a tight loop.

claims.statement: Backoff delay is capped at policy.maxMs.
withRetry sleeps between attempts but not after the final one.
The blocking busy-wait sleep helper is removed.
The retry guide describes the new signature and backoff.

decisions.chosen: Pass retry settings as an options object.

risks.concern: Callers passing a positional attempts count silently get the default of 3.

evidence.observation: test/backoff.test.js covers growth and the cap for delayFor.
No test exercises withRetry's sleep between attempts.

stops.title: Introduce a capped backoff policy
stops.intro: A new module owns the backoff math. Everything else in this tour builds on it, so it comes first.

beats.say: The defaults: start at 100 ms, double each attempt, never exceed two seconds.
The cap is enforced here, in the policy, so no caller can forget it.

qa.answer: The commit doesn't say. My inference: two seconds keeps the worst case for five attempts under ten seconds, which fits a typical request timeout. Treat that as reconstruction, not stated intent.
There's no jitter. Many clients failing together will retry in lockstep. That's worth a concern if this runs at scale.

stops.title: withRetry sleeps between attempts
stops.intro: This stop carries the risk: withRetry's signature changed shape.

beats.say: Before, attempts was positional. Removed code opens in the pinned diff, with a read-only base companion beside it in inline layouts.
Now it's an options object. A caller still passing a number gets the default of three, with no error.
The sleep is skipped after the final attempt, so a hard failure isn't delayed for nothing.

focus.note: no sleep after the last try

beats.say: The only in-repo caller was updated in the same commit.

qa.answer: I searched for `withRetry(`. src/client.js:6 is the only caller, and it's updated in this diff. Callers outside this repository would silently fall back to three attempts.
`i < attempts - 1` skips the sleep after the final attempt. Without it, a caller that exhausts retries would wait one extra backoff before seeing the error.

stops.title: Remove the busy-wait sleep
stops.intro: A deleted file. It only has a base side.

beats.say: This spun the CPU for the whole delay. The promise-based sleep in retry.js yields instead.

qa.answer: Nothing in the base revision required legacy-sleep.js. It was already dead code, so deleting it is safe.

stops.title: Rename and update the retry guide
stops.intro: A renamed file: docs/RETRY.md became docs/retries.md, with two lines rewritten.

beats.say: The old text, read from the old path at the base revision.
The new text matches the options signature and the backoff.

qa.answer: My inference is that it matches the lowercase naming of the other docs. Nothing in the repository links to the old path, so no references broke.

stops.title: What the tests do and don't cover
stops.intro: An added test file. It has no base side, so it always opens as a file.

beats.say: Growth and the cap are asserted directly.
Nothing asserts that withRetry actually waits between attempts. I've recorded that as missing evidence, not as a pass.

qa.answer: With node:test's mock timers: enable them, call withRetry with a function that fails twice, then advance the clock by 100 ms and 200 ms and assert the call count after each tick.
The commit message says only "Cap retry backoff and sleep between attempts". My reading: back-to-back retries were hammering a struggling dependency. That's inferred, not stated.
The main risk is the signature change in stop 2: positional callers silently get three attempts. Second is the missing timing test in stop 5.
delayFor is unit-tested; withRetry's sleeping is not. Stop 5 covers it.

closing: End to end, retries stop hammering the dependency: a capped exponential policy, a non-blocking sleep between attempts, the busy-wait helper gone, and the guide updated. The signature change is the part to watch.
